items.title: Earl King Interview, 1980-04-10
items.q: I saw how Baptiste do a thing on Little Willie John with 22 pieces... And I think that's phenomenal.

ctx.x: and all that kind of thing. But that's been one reason why the bandit companies came from out of town, because they didn't take it.

Right, they didn't have to get up with all the red tape that they had to go through with the musician. Plus, they get the finished product. You know, they say, hey, we go to New Orleans, the guy arrange the thing, we conduct it, and get the job done, you know, and it's that. I saw how Baptiste do a thing on Little Willie John with 22 pieces, eight of range, not a stitch of music. And I think that's phenomenal. 22, because you can run into some clashes.
I wanted to know if Harold Baptiste was the brains behind, what you call him, the brains behind? The brains behind? Yes. Oh, anybody.

items.title: Earl King Interview, 1980-04-10
items.q: We were talking about barely with the Howard Baptiste thing. Uh, uh, where things were getting ready to change. And the rhythm content in the music was so structured to what he was saying was irrelevant.

ctx.x: Anyone else? Anyone else? Yes, George. Yeah, George. He needs to keep his hand up. George. Yeah. But some of the things that we've done throughout the years and where our new music is today, where we know it came from, we think there's a market for things like some of the newer things that, you know, where New Orleans music is now. Yeah, I'm glad you touched upon it. Maybe you can bring that into perspective.

Where are we now? Where are we going? Because, you know, where are we going? Yeah. Well, right now, man, we're on the borderline, nationally, I would say we're on the borderline of making our transition to music. We are listening at disco. But what George is asking the question, in the marketplace in America, we deal with consciousness of people who are listening at music, people listening to music, they hear what you give them. If you've got good product, I think New Orleans at the market. If the product is…
